question: Does a reviewer prompt that names the re-derivation class (a fact established at T1 is re-derived at T2 from something that can change in between) and tells the reviewer to enumerate every re-lookup and attack the window between establishment and use find more of the known defects than no prompt at all?
why_after_a_null: The first prompt eval (3429f759ceef) was null: -3.3 pp, 95% [-18.8, +9.5]. Its candidate told the reviewer how to work (read, list claims, probe). This candidate tells a running reviewer what to attack. The hypothesis comes from the latest round of five pull requests, where one class dominated.

inherits.runner: run.ts, with one added arm entry `rederive`
inherits.note: Detection (`detects`, window_chars 1200, every mechanism and trigger group inside one window), exclusion of errored runs, the per-arm Wilson and cluster-bootstrap intervals and the paired cluster bootstrap over (head, trial) pairs are the first eval's code, unchanged. grade.ts, rounds.ts and cases.json hash to the values the rounds freeze recorded.

candidate.length_rule: The control arm appends 0 characters, so 'no longer than the control' cannot be met literally. The candidate is held to the strictest non-empty reading: no longer than the shipped reviewer prompt (prompts/current.md, 3349 characters), and so also shorter than the first eval's candidate (4797).
candidate.written_from: The class statement and the ten example shapes given in the lane assignment, generalised: it names no repository identifier and no finding. It was written before any corpus record was classified and before any stratum-B record or case existed.
candidate.tuning: None. One version, run once. A null result is reported as a null result.

A.name: original
A.cases: cases.json, unchanged: 30 findings over pr17394-r7, pr17394-r8, pr17399-r3
A.classification: all 197 corpus findings are labelled; the 30 cases are the subset with runs

B.name: batch extension
B.rule: Every finding the latest completed cross-family review round reports as open on its head, for each of the five pull requests in the current fix batch, at 2026-10-30T12:00Z. Rounds still running at that time are excluded.
B.excluded_running: #17394 round 17, #17398 round 20, #17412 round 8 and #17421 round 18 were still running at the cut.
B.cases: cases-b.json, written from the records by agents that were not shown the candidate prompt or the hypothesis, and frozen and committed before the first stratum-B model call
B.diff_base: the merge-base of each head with upstream/main
B.snapshots: git archive of the full head sha, root node_modules entries linked to the first eval's dependency donor (bun.lock and every package.json are identical to pr17399-r3), @oh-my-pi workspace links pointing into the snapshot itself, the native addon linked from the donor, then made read-only
B.in_sample_warning: The class was named from these rounds. Stratum B is the hypothesis-generating set, so a gain there is weaker evidence than a gain on A, and is never reported without saying so.

arms.name: control
arms.role: control, run fresh beside the candidate

arms.name: candidate
arms.role: attribution: the first eval's probe-first prompt, run fresh, to tell naming the class apart from any prompt that makes the reviewer run probes

held_fixed.trials_reason: The first eval's 2 trials per head gave a paired interval 28 pp wide on 6 pairs. 4 trials keep the design and the bootstrap and give 12 pairs on A and 20 on B. The pairing unit and every formula are unchanged.
held_fixed.max_cost_reason: A safety cap, the same for every arm. The first eval's same-family runs never reached $3; a run that reaches the cap exits 3 and is excluded and counted, never scored zero.
held_fixed.bun_on_path: /home/sami/.mise/installs/bun/1.4.4/bin first on PATH for every arm
held_fixed.arms_interleaved: Arms run in the same time window, so provider drift and box load fall on all arms alike.

primary.name: A
primary.reads: like for like with the first eval's -3.3 pp: does naming the class find more on cases the class was not named from

primary.name: B
primary.reads: the same on the rounds the class was named from

secondary.name: class subgroup
secondary.test: rederive - control on the findings labelled `instance` only, and on the rest

secondary.name: continuity
secondary.test: rederive (this lane) against the first eval's stored control runs, unpaired rates

secondary.name: pooled
secondary.test: rederive - control over A and B together, always labelled pooled

comparisons.null_rule: A comparison is a null result when its 95% paired interval contains 0.
comparisons.reading_rule: The lever is supported only if primary A excludes 0. Primary B excluding 0 with A null is an in-sample result and is reported as that.

intervals.per_arm: Wilson over (finding, run) pairs and a cluster bootstrap over runs, grade.ts, 10000 iterations, seed 20261030
intervals.paired: rounds.ts pairedCompare: cluster bootstrap over (head, trial) pairs, 10000 iterations, seed 20261030
intervals.report_rule: n and the 95% interval always; never a bare delta

classification.labellers: two independent labellers from different model families, each labelling every record of both strata without seeing the other's labels or any run; disagreements are adjudicated against the rubric with the reason recorded
classification.agreement: raw agreement and Cohen's kappa on the three labels and on instance against the rest
classification.reported: the share of `instance` findings in the 197-finding corpus, in the 30 cases, and in stratum B, each with a Wilson interval
